data.name: Nidhra
data.gender_notes: Nidhra is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The one who sleeps or rests, derived from the root word 'nidh' meaning 'to sleep'. In Hindu mythology, Nidhra is a goddess of sleep and dreams. The name Nidhra carries the meaning “Sleep, Rest” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Nidhra usually hope their child will grow to embody sleep, rest and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Nidhra belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sleep, Rest.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nidhra total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: In Hindu culture, a good night's sleep is considered essential for good health and well-being. Nidhra, the goddess of sleep, is revered for her ability to grant peace and rest. She is depicted as lying on a bed of serpents or a cushioned bed, holding a lamp and a fan, symbolizing the cooling night breeze. Her name is used in various Hindu rituals and prayers, seeking her blessings for a restful sleep.
data.spiritual_significance: Nidhra represents the peaceful and restful aspect of the divine. In Hindu philosophy, sleep is seen as a chance to detach from the material world and connect with the inner self. The spiritual significance of the name Nidhra lies in its association with rest and relaxation, allowing one to recharge and prepare for the daily spiritual journey. It is a reminder to prioritize self-care and sleep, not just for physical health, but also for mental and emotional well-being.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nidhra, meaning 'sleep' or 'rest', symbolizes the tranquil repose of the soul. It encourages one to seek inner peace, away from the hustle and bustle of worldly life, and to rejuvenate in the arms of the divine.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Nidhra is a name of a goddess in Hindu mythology. The name Nidhra carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
